title: Alignment Conservers exist so SKY holders can vote in their own long-term interest despite low individual alignment
content:
A.0.1.1.17 defines Alignment Conservers as external entities that facilitate and protect the Sky Governance process by ensuring it occurs according to the processes defined in the Atlas.

The operative clause is the rationale: ACs "enable SKY holders to participate in Sky Governance in a manner where it is easy for SKY holders to make the decisions that best benefit their long-term interests as SKY holders, **even if SKY holders overall have relatively little alignment**."

This is Alignment Artifact Strength applied to the electorate. Rather than assuming or demanding an aligned voter base, the design lowers the alignment threshold required to vote well — the same move as strengthening an Artifact so less Inner Incentive is needed. ACs are the institutional mechanism for that floor-raising in governance specifically.

Aligned Delegates (A.0.1.1.18) are then a specific AC form: anonymous, using Delegate Contracts to hold delegated voting power. The Atlas flags them as "both highly influential and potentially risky" precisely because they concentrate incentivized voting power, and commits to derisking tools rather than trusting them.
description: ACs are external entities that police adherence to Atlas process; their purpose is making well-aligned choices EASY for holders rather than requiring holders to be aligned.
